name: mio_basic
kind: survey: result latency, issue spacing and queue behaviour of the variable-latency producers that go through the SM's MIO path (S2R, S2UR, CS2R, LDC, ULDC / LDCU, LDS, SHFL, VOTE, R2UR), alone, in runs and mixed, at 1 to 16 warps per SM; installs nothing
mechanisms: instruction.service (S2R, S2UR, CS2R, LDC, ULDC, LDCU, LDS, SHFL.*, VOTE, R2UR: result latency, issue interval, resource)
why: Step 3 of dev/design/stall-attribution.md. The largest attribution gaps left on the full-GPU sets (full-bb2b) are in these classes: long_scoreboard -2.8 / -2.7, mio_throttle -2.4 (H100), short_scoreboard -1.3 / -2.3 (loop) and -1.7 (outside, H100) points of residency; the replay has no bounded queue at all (no reason maps to mio_throttle except tma / shfl unit waits).
data_seen_before_freezing: Leaves (instruction.service, both trees): S2R 23 / 23, S2UR 35 / 35, CS2R 14 (h100; b300 placeholder 1), LDS 21.95 / 21.99, SHFL.BFLY 24 (interval 3.99) on both, SHFL.IDX 26.0, VOTE 13 (interval 2.0), R2UR 4 (h100; b300 placeholder 1), LDC / ULDC / LDCU 1 with the constant paths of constant_paths v1 / v2 on top; resources alu_smsp / uniform_smsp / lsu_smsp / shfl_smsp, no in-flight bound anywhere.

Loop kernels of sync_basic / branch_basic (per execution, hardware / replay): reader of S2UR SR_CLOCKLO short_scoreboard 32.1-33.7 / 32-33 on both devices (right); reader of a resident LDC in u.bar_late3 22.2 / 14.1 on h100; reader of LDCU 9.95 / 10.0 on b300; warp_issue v3: a batch of constant loads is served serially at 31.5 cycles per line and LDCs behind the fourth wait at issue as mio_throttle; sync_basic v2: at 8 warps the SYNCS instructions carry mio_throttle 32.7 / 22.0 per iteration (a bounded queue in front of the per-SM server). No cell isolates one of these producers with an adjacent reader, a run of them, or two kinds mixed.

probe.chain: tools/microbench/sync_basic harness (cells.tsv, probe/, build.sh, loop gate, run.sh, derive.py; case names mb-sb-<cell>; set mio_basic; build dir $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/mio_basic/<device>/build), plan cells generated like the v cells of branch_basic v1 (gen_v.py pattern): PTX frame -> ptxas -O3 -> free-mode sass_patch plan -> nvdisasm listing -> ptx_runner; capture, two reference passes, replay with build 68702860.
probe.frame m: m.loop.ptx: loop of N = 64 iterations with a run-time bound, body = 16 filler pairs (S = 32 filler slots per iteration after ptxas, unrolling taken as it comes), a shared-memory word per thread initialised before the loop, clocks before and after; stores t0, t1, the iteration count (check word, must be 64) and the scratch register. A plan rewrites the filler slots of every unrolled copy identically. Slots that are not named keep a NOP with the stall field of the instruction they replace (branch_basic v1 lesson); the counter, compare, branch and label words stay. Producer and reader words come from a donor function of the same module (never launched) or from operand synthesis.
probe.pattern: A run of n producers P occupies consecutive slots starting behind the frame's compare (no producer between the counter add and its compare); every producer has stall 1, yield bit 1, writes its own destination register and raises dependency barrier 0; one reader R (an integer add of the last destination into the scratch register, wait mask bit 0, stall 1) follows the last producer directly; the rest of the iteration is NOP. Destinations are not read otherwise.

producers.s2ur: S2UR URx, SR_CTAID.X (reader: add of the uniform register)
producers.ldc: LDC Rx, c[0x0][<a kernel parameter word>] (one line, resident after the first iteration)
producers.uldc: ULDC URx, c[0x0][..] on sm_90a / LDCU URx, c[0x0][..] on sm_103a (the form ptxas emits on the target)
producers.lds: LDS Rx, [Rbase] from the thread's shared word (Rbase set before the loop)

cells.m.nop: all slots NOP: the frame. Shapes 1, 4, 8, 16 warps per CTA (one CTA per SM).
cells.m.<p>.n1 / .n4 / .n8 / .n16: runs of 1, 4, 8, 16 producers of kind p, for each of the ten producers, 1 warp per CTA.
cells.m.<p>.n8.w4 / .w8 / .w16: the run of 8 at 4, 8, 16 warps per CTA for p in s2r, lds, shfl_bfly, ldc.
cells.m.mix.s2r_lds.n8, m.mix.lds_shfl.n8, m.m: runs of 8 alternating the two kinds (4 + 4), reader behind the last, 1 warp.
cells.unrealised: a producer form that cannot be placed (synthesis or donor fails, or the patched word does not decode) is recorded in tools/microbench/mio_basic/unrealised.txt before the run and its cells are left out; the definition is not bent.

derivation.per cell: clock period per iteration (launches 0 and 2), sample total and extended total per iteration (loop pcs plus the pc behind the loop), per-pc hardware classes against replay reasons.
derivation.latency:
L(p) = hardware residency per execution on the reader of m.

.n1 minus the reader's residency in a run where it does not wait (its stall): issue of the producer to issue of the reader, less 1.
derivation.spacing and queue: T(p, n) = sample total - m.nop; spacing(p) = (T(p,16) - T(p,8)) / 8 and (T(p,8) - T(p,4)) / 4; the classes on the producers (mio_throttle, short_scoreboard, wait) and the first n at which mio_throttle appears; from the w cells T per warp against warps per SM and per SMSP.
derivation.mix: T(mix) against the mean of the two pure runs of 8: equal = one queue shared by the two kinds at the slower spacing or independent paths; the classes say which.

questions_before_data.Q1 (latency): Is each producer's issue-to-reader time the installed result latency (S2R 23, S2UR 35, CS2R 14, LDS 22, SHFL.BFLY 24, SHFL.IDX 26, VOTE 13, R2UR 4, resident LDC / ULDC / LDCU per constant_paths) on both devices? B300 CS2R, R2UR are placeholders.
questions_before_data.Q2 (spacing): Candidates per producer: (S-a) issue is free and results return one latency after each issue (T grows by the stall only: 1 per producer); (S-b) a serial server: T grows by a fixed spacing per producer (the installed intervals: SHFL 4, VOTE 2, S2R 2, 31.5 per constant line); (S-c) a bounded queue: free up to a depth d, then the producers wait at issue (mio_throttle) at the server's rate.
questions_before_data.Q3 (scope): Is the server / queue per warp, per SMSP or per SM (w cells: T per warp constant, growing from 2 warps per SMSP, or growing with warps per SM)?
questions_before_data.Q4 (sharing): Do S2R, LDS, SHFL, LDC, S2UR share one queue / server (mix cells), as the hardware's single MIO class suggests, or do they run on separate paths as the replay's resources (alu_smsp, lsu_smsp, shfl_smsp, uniform_smsp) have it?

install: Nothing. Readings go into the addenda; an installation protocol follows.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value; no cell dropped after its data is seen.

addenda.when: 2026-11-17, h100 and b300 runs, third root (56 cells each; $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/mio_basic-r3/<device>; tables mio_basic-readings/{read-r3-<device>.txt, T-table.txt} from tools/microbench/mio_basic/readings.py; replay build 68702860) - readings; nothing installed
addenda.text: VALIDITY. r2ur is unrealised on both targets (ptxas only emits it predicated). Root mio_basic (first run) is void: producer destinations lay beyond the function's register count (illegal instruction); the frame now keeps 44 registers live (7596edf1). Root mio_basic-r2 is void for the replay: the pool began with R1, the stack pointer the tracer's instrumentation saves through, so every traced launch with an ordinary-register producer faulted (direct runs were right); R0-R9 are excluded now (48d8dee3 / b3dba748; the plans of the two commits are identical, the launch clone was advanced from the first to the second during the run, which changed no probe file). In mio_basic-r3 all 56 cells of both devices have right check words, complete traces and ledgers. The loop listings inside the reused probe build dir are stale (old frame); the readings use listings regenerated from the run's own SASS (mio_basic-readings/loops-<device>). The b300 one-warp clock of m.nop is 8.6 above its sample total (148.3 against 135.9; the 4-warp clock is 139.7), so the b300 values below are from the samples. QUANTITY. T(p, n) = extended sample total - m.nop of the same shape + 3 (n + 1): the cycles beyond the stall-1 issue of the n producers and the reader (each replaced a stall-4 NOP). The reader sits directly behind the last producer. READINGS, h100 / b300, T at n = 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 (replay h100 | b300 in brackets). S2R: 0 / 25.3 / 29.0 / 36.4 and 0 / 25.4 / 29.5 / 37.4 (22, 25, 29, 37 | 0, 22, 22, 22). LDS: 1 / 24.8 / 28.3 / 36.3 and 1 / 25.1 / 27.8 / 36.9 (0, 25, 29, 37 | 0, 21, 21, 21). SHFL.BFLY: 0 / 25.9 / 29.8 / 38.3 and 0 / 26.8 / 29.9 / 40.9 (0, 32, 44, 68 on both). SHFL.IDX: 0 / 33.5 / 45.8 / 69.5 and 0 / 32.5 / 46.5 / 68.4 (0, 34, 46, 70 on both). S2UR: 0 / 36.6 / 41.7 / 55.6 and 1.5 / 37.4 / 42.8 / 56.8 (0, 37, 41, 49 | 0, 34, 34, 34). LDC (resident line): -0.7 / 27.6 / 32.0 / 40.1 and 1.9 / 31.6 / 32.4 / 39.0 (0, 22, 22, 22 | 0, 27, 27, 27). ULDC (h100): 0 at every n (replay 0). LDCU (b300): 0.4 / 17.3 / 21.9 / 29.4 (0, 18, 18, 18). CS2R: 0.8 / 3.2 / 8.1 / 15.6 and 1.1 / 5.1 / 8.5 / 16.9 (13, 28, 48, 88 | 0, 0, 0, 0). VOTE: 0.4 / 5.3 / 8.2 / 16.4 and 1.1 / 4.7 / 8.2 / 17.3 (0, 15, 19, 27 on both). Q1 / Q2 (latency and spacing). (i) With one producer the reader does not wait at all on either device, for every kind: a reader one cycle behind the producer does not yet see the raised dependency barrier (issue_rules v1: visible one cycle after the raise); from n = 4 on it waits for the producers it does see, as short_scoreboard. The replay agrees except h100 S2R (22: the installed issue interval 2 on the ALU unit moves the reader one cycle back, where it sees the barrier) and h100 CS2R. (ii) S2R, LDS, SHFL.BFLY: T = 21-22 + n on both devices, i.e. the results of a run return 2 cycles apart behind a first latency of about 25 (reader issue at 21-22 + 2 n after the first producer's issue). The h100 replay has exactly this for S2R and LDS and 4 apart for SHFL.BFLY (too slow); the b300 replay has no spacing for S2R and LDS (interval 0 in its leaves) and 4 for SHFL.BFLY. (iii) SHFL.IDX: 4 apart (T = 21.5 + 3 n) on both devices; the replay is right. (iv) S2UR: 33 + n up to 8, then 6-7 more at 16 with mio_throttle on the producers (4 per iteration at n = 8, 12 at n = 16): a bounded queue (S-c), about 6-8 deep; the replay has no bound (h100 49 against 55.6) and no spacing on b300. (v) Resident LDC: 23.6 + n (h100), reader wait constant at 28 while the producers take mio_throttle 4 (n = 8) and 12 (n = 16): the same bound; b300 31.6 / 32.4 / 39.0. The replay is flat (22 / 27). (vi) ULDC on h100 is a fixed-latency instruction: its reader never waits. LDCU on b300: 13.5 + n, reader wait constant 17; replay flat 18. (vii) CS2R and VOTE: T = n and the reader does not wait: 2 cycles per instruction with math_pipe_throttle on the next one, an execution-unit interval and no barrier wait. The replay gives CS2R result latency 14 and interval 6 on h100 (88 at n = 16 against 15.6) and a placeholder on b300 (0 against 16.9), and gives VOTE a 13-cycle wait on the reader (27 against 16.4). Q3 (scope), runs of 8 at 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 warps per CTA, T: S2R 29.0 / 30.0 / 33.4 / 134.8 (h100), 29.5 / 31.7 / 37.1 / 138.7 (b300); LDC 32.0 / 36.5 / 40.2 / 136.6 and 32.4 / 43.3 / 42.8 / 138.5; LDS 28.3 / 30.7 / 33.5 / 48.8 and 27.8 / 43.4 / 45.0 / 50.4; SHFL.BFLY 29.8 / 37.5 / 34.6 / 48.8 and 29.9 / 44.3 / 46.4 / 52.2. At 16 warps the S2R and LDC periods are 257 cycles = 128 producers on the SM x 2.0: one server per SM for S2R and LDC at 2 cycles per instruction, with mio_throttle on the producers (21.6 / 71.3 per iteration) and the rest on the reader. LDS and SHFL.BFLY do not saturate (period 170 at 128 instructions per SM): their spacing is not per SM (per SMSP or per warp; not separated: 32 per SMSP x 2 = 64 is below the period). b300 LDS and SHFL.BFLY step up by 13-15 from 1 to 4 warps (h100: 2 and 8, the latter with clock and samples disagreeing by 7): unexplained. Replay at 16 warps: S2R 59.8 / 37.4, LDC 39.0 / 43.2 (no per-SM server), LDS 46.8 / 38.4, SHFL.BFLY 45.8 / 46.1. Q4 (sharing), runs of 4 + 4 alternating: S2R + LDS 28.5 / 29.9 (pure runs of 8: 29.0 and 28.3), LDS + SHFL.BFLY 28.9 / 30.2 (28.3, 29.8): within one warp these kinds queue behind each other like one kind; S2R + S2UR 33.6 / 33.2 (29.0, 41.7) and LDC + S2R 24.9 / 25.5 (32.0, 29.0) lie between or below the pure runs (the last producer the reader sees differs), not separable into shared / independent with these cells. Replay h100: 22 / 29 / 34 / 23 (S2R + LDS too fast: its two kinds run on separate units). OPEN for the installation protocol: the first latency (25 from the first issue to the first result in a run, against leaves 23 / 22 / 24); which producers the per-SM server holds besides S2R and LDC (S2UR, LDCU not run at several warps); the depth of the bound in front of it; the scope of the LDS / SHFL spacing; the b300 step at 4 warps.
